To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrical properties of ohmic contacts to N-polar nGaN depend on carrier concentration and annealing temperature, and ohmic contacts can be formed on samples with carrier concentration above 2.0×1019cm−3, even when the samples are annealed at 700°C.

Ti/Al ohmic contacts to N-polar nGaN can be formed at 500°C or 700°C for samples with carrier concentrations of 2.2 × 1018 cm-3 or 2.0× 1019 cm-3, respectively, and that the formation and degradation of the ohmic contacts are attributed to the formation of an interfacial w- AlN layer.
the ohmic contact degradation mechanism is different from that of P-GaN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of N-polar n- and p-type GaN.
the electrical characteristics and ohmic contact degradation mechanisms of Ti/Al contacts to n-GaN, which is critical for the development of vertical-structure light-emitting diodes.
the effect of the annealing temperature and the carrier concentration on the Ti/Al contacts to N-polar n- and p-GaN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ohmic contacts to N-polar n-nGaN are formed by a reaction between Al and the N atoms in the top surface layer of GaN and the formation of an AlN layer at the interface.

the ohmic contact behavior of the Ti/Al ohmic contacts is determined by the formation of a wurtzize AlN interfacial layer, which is in turn controlled by the annealing temperature and the GaN carrier concentration.
, for samples annealed at 700°C with carrier concentration of ∼1018 cm-3, an interfacial layer of AlN with a thickness of ∼4  nm formed, which is responsible for the ohmic behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ohmic contact degradation mechanism is related to GaN decomposition at high temperatures, and the ohmic contact is formed via the formation of an interfacial wirtzite AlN.
, for samples grown by the same method, the electrical properties of N-polar GaN are strongly dependent on the carrier concentration.
the ohmic contact degradation mechanism of Ti/Al contacts on n-GaN with carrier concentration of ∼1018 cm-3 is different from that on n-GaN of ∼1019 cm-3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for Ti/Al ohmic contacts to N-polar nGaN, the formation and thickness of the interfacial AlN layer play an important role in the contact resistance.
, for N-polar n-contacts to n-type GaN with carrier concentrations below 1019 cm3, the ohmic behavior can be obtained when the interfacial w-GaN thickness is reduced to a few nanometers.
the ohmic contact degradation mechanism for Ti/Al contacts to n-GaN is not the same for N-polar and c-polar n-GaNs.
